_comment: The task catalog. This file is the only thing that needs editing to add a
capability: drop a script in src/scripts/ and describe it here. The router
prompt and the executor both read from this file, so neither needs code
changes.
id             - what the model selects. Stable; treat it as an API name.
type           - powershell | python | builtin | noop
executor       - script filename in src/scripts/, or the builtin's name
description    - shown to the router model; this is what drives routing
allow_args     - the task accepts arguments at all (default false)
args_allowlist - every supplied arg must appear here verbatim. Only list
flags that are safe in any combination; anything taking
a free-form value cannot be allowlisted this way.
errors         - optional {exit_code: name}. Turns a script's exit code
into a named reason the caller can act on, instead of
the default 'task_failed: exit N'.
args_pattern   - optional regex. An arg not in args_allowlist is accepted
when it matches this. For values that cannot be listed
up front, like an application name. Keep it tight: no
quotes, semicolons or pipes, and a length limit.
routable       - set false to hide a task from the router. It can still
be run directly by the service. Use for anything with
side effects that a model must not choose on its own.
Script-backed tasks whose file is missing are hidden from the router until
the script exists, so an entry can be added before it is implemented.

tasks.description: The application or window the user is focused on right now: what they are currently working on, what is in the foreground, what is open on screen. Returns the app name by default; pass -Format json for the window title, process id and idle seconds as well.

The user's Microsoft Teams and Outlook calendar: meetings, calls, and appointments that are scheduled or coming up. Use for anything about their schedule - whether they have a call soon, what their next meeting is, what is on today or this week, whether they are free, who organized a meeting, or whether a call is happening right now. Returns each upcoming event with its start time and how many minutes away it is. Pass -Window with next3h for the next few hours, today for the rest of today, next24h for the next day, or week for the next seven days.

Start, open, launch or run an application on this machine: 'open Chrome', 'start Notepad', 'launch Spotify', 'can you open VS Code'. Also answers whether an application is installed. Pass -Name followed by the application the user named.
Install an application with winget. Never routed: the service runs this only after the user has explicitly agreed to an install it offered.
Collect application and system logs for diagnostics: log files, recent errors, crashes, traces.
Details about the machine itself: operating system, release, CPU architecture, Python version, hardware specs.
Liveness check. Also the fallback for any query that does not match another task: greetings, chit-chat, ambiguous or empty input.
